assumptions: The initial product does not determine conformity or certify machinery; a qualified machinery-safety professional retains all technical judgments and the related contractual responsibility.
A narrowly defined machine or robot-cell category exists in which engineering artefacts and handover steps are repeatable enough to support reusable integrations.
The proposed pricing, handover volume, 55-75% blended gross margin, sales cycle, and retention are planning hypotheses rather than validated operating results.
Integrators can lawfully and securely grant access to the required PLC, safety-program, drawing, and component-version artefacts.
The founder can keep the pilot within 15-20 hours per week only if onboarding and specialist review are standardized and materially delegated.
The research does not establish that incumbents lack configuration-provenance integrations or that buyers regard this gap as important enough to adopt another system.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The as-designed versus as-commissioned divergence is a coherent operational failure, and a signed configuration baseline is a precise control point tied to real documentation duties. The insight is weakened because the frequency and cost of the failure are unmeasured and the claimed PLC-level gap in incumbent workflows remains unverified.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Machinery safety, delayed acceptance, and defective technical files can carry meaningful regulatory and project consequences, while incumbent software and consulting prices demonstrate an existing compliance budget. There is no evidence yet of how often file divergence causes losses or that integrators will pay for a separate provenance layer rather than use current CE, PLM, or project tools.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Subscription revenue plus paid handover review can create repeat revenue, the proposed initial capital is affordable, and the stated pricing has some grounding in incumbent spend. However, lower-priced substitutes constrain SaaS pricing, qualified review and integration keep blended margins below pure software levels, and CAC, onboarding effort, sales-cycle length, retention, handover frequency, payback, and the 150-customer wealth path are all unvalidated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish automation integrators delivering a single repeatable machine class form a reasonably focused initial buyer group with recurring handover events. The first machine category has not been selected, and there is no evidence for the number of reachable integrators, qualifying projects per year, or whether the Polish beachhead alone is economically meaningful.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Owning the release gate could create a valuable workflow position, but Safexpert, CEM4, CEDOC, Pilz, and existing engineering systems already cover much of the documentation, history, collaboration, and expert-service stack. With no demonstrated configuration-ingestion gap, exclusive channel, or switching trigger, a particularly strong position in the beachhead is presently unlikely.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven release workflow could extend to additional machine classes, later modifications, owner-side asset records, more engineering connectors, and other EU markets. Expansion is plausible but depends on whether artefact schemas, safety processes, and integrations transfer across heterogeneous machines without recreating costly services for each segment.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Integrator-specific mappings, accepted evidence templates, configuration history, and workflow embedding could produce switching costs and improve with use. Those assets begin at zero, customers may resist centralizing sensitive intellectual property, and established compliance or PLM vendors could add similar connectors without facing an obvious proprietary barrier.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Automatic binding of exact PLC and safety-program versions to a signed release packet could improve accuracy and reduce manual reconciliation. The research does not show that incumbents fail to provide this capability, quantify the time or risk reduction, or establish an advantage large enough to justify another system and integration project.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The Machinery Regulation becoming mandatory on 20 January 2027 creates a near-term review window, and its attention to software, AI, cyber-safety, and modification duties makes configuration evidence more salient. The benefit is tempered because established vendors and consultancies are already positioned to absorb the same demand.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Referrals from machinery-safety assessors and embedding in an integrator commissioning checklist are credible channel hypotheses, and the founder has regional industrial access. No assessor or association has committed, the offer requires high trust and sensitive-system access, and long consultative sales plus integration work may make acquisition expensive and difficult to scale part-time.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data-lineage and automation skills fit the product, the proposed capital is within reach, and a narrow pilot can in principle be run part-time with a contractor. Execution still requires machinery-safety expertise, secure access to customer intellectual property, reliable integrations, careful liability boundaries, and enterprise onboarding while founder time is already near its stated ceiling.

main_structural_strength: A specific, recurring control point—the signed as-built configuration baseline at machine handover—links a high-stakes compliance workflow to data-lineage automation and can generate both subscription and event-based revenue.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed provenance wedge is not demonstrated to be missing from incumbent CE or engineering systems, so buyers may see a separate, integration-heavy release layer as duplicative; this compounds weak differentiation with slow distribution and service-heavy economics.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Safexpert already advertises change tracking, traceable histories, reusable projects, teamwork, standards monitoring, and technical-documentation workflows, while CEM4, CEDOC, and Pilz add low-priced software and expert or end-to-end services; the research found no direct evidence that automatic PLC and safety-program provenance is an uncovered, budgeted gap.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots in one repeatable machine class should show the baseline rate and cost of as-built divergence, successful secure ingestion of PLC and safety-program version evidence, a material reduction in handover time or defects versus incumbent workflows, buyer willingness to pay at the proposed price, bounded onboarding and review hours, a repeatable assessor-led acquisition channel, and renewal or repeat-handover behavior.
highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the business to an embedded, vendor-neutral release connector for one high-volume PLC/robot-cell stack and distribute it as a white-label module through qualified assessors or integrators, with automated evidence ingestion as the product and specialist review optional; this would target the only potentially distinct gap while reducing standalone-sales friction and human-service load.
